answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-2: the Registry refuses first registration of new combustion cars.

question.text: Will the legal sellers comply with the ban (stop selling openly)?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-4: some would-be buyers of new combustion cars rank a used car or keeping their present car above a new BEV or PHEV.

question.text: Will a meaningful share of buyers keep wanting the good after the ban?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-14: residents evade the ban by keeping combustion cars registered in Drevland (the nearest row; below the cut-off).

question.text: Will many informal sales go undetected?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: registration is refused, selling an unregistrable new car as new is an offence with a $5,000 fine, and registration is required to drive legally.

question.text: Will enforcement be active enough that informal sellers face a real risk of punishment?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: the 12 importers and 600 dealers can sell BEVs, PHEVs and used cars; the Act bans only one engine type in new cars.

question.text: Are the legal sellers unable to replace the banned good with other products for most of their business?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-25: some would-be buyers of combustion cars buy PHEVs in 2035 to 2037 (BEVs are a substitute too).

question.text: Are some legal substitutes acceptable to some buyers?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-15: dealers, fuel retailers and motoring clubs, and BEV importers and charging firms, can each organize at a cost below their stake in the review.

question.text: Can the former legal sellers or the buyers organize to seek repeal at a cost below their stake?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-7: buyers know the date, and some can bring the purchase of a new combustion car forward into 2033 to 2034.

question.text: Can the buyers or importers buy ahead of the effective date, by storing the good or placing orders early?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: the same Registry refuses first registration; the text gives no reason to expect less compliance for PHEVs after 2038 (compare A-2 for K1, 0.95).

question.text: Will the legal sellers comply with the ban (stop selling openly)?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: PHEVs are the closest to combustion cars in range and refueling, so some buyers will still want one after 2038; BEVs will be cheaper by then.

question.text: Will a meaningful share of buyers keep wanting the good after the ban?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: the same registration route as K1; the text gives no sign of undetected sales (compare A-14, 0.3).

question.text: Will many informal sales go undetected?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: same enforcement as K1: refused registration and a $5,000 fine.

question.text: Will enforcement be active enough that informal sellers face a real risk of punishment?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: importers and dealers keep selling BEVs and used cars.

question.text: Are the legal sellers unable to replace the banned good with other products for most of their business?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: BEVs, used cars and keeping the present car are open to buyers of new PHEVs.

question.text: Are some legal substitutes acceptable to some buyers?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: the same dealers and importers who can organize on K1 (A-15, 0.85) have a stake in the PHEV date.

question.text: Can the former legal sellers or the buyers organize to seek repeal at a cost below their stake?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-050; judged from the text: buyers know the 2038 date; the text gives no PHEV-specific rush, but replacement cycles of 6 to 10 years (A-7 for combustion cars, 0.85) make buying ahead feasible.

question.text: Can the buyers or importers buy ahead of the effective date, by storing the good or placing orders early?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-050 (illustrative figures), A-21: under U1-b, registering a new combustion car briefly in Drevland and importing it costs less than the premium it earns in Vessmark for some importers.

question.text: For some of the actors bound by the measure, will reshaping goods so that they fall outside the measure's definitions cost less than the measure would cost them?

source_sentences: From 1 January 2035 the Registry shall not register for the first time a new passenger car fitted with an internal combustion engine.
'new passenger car' means a passenger car that has not previously been registered.
Nothing in this Act affects the use, sale, transfer or re-registration of a car registered before the date in section 3 or 4.
Registration is refused; selling an unregistrable new car as new is an offence, fine $5,000.
The Registry's budget is fixed by law; no new funds.
The bill was introduced on 3 March 2026, passed on 18 June 2026 by a large cross-party majority, and enacted on 30 June 2026.
plug-in hybrids with at least 50 km of electric range are exempt until 31 December 2037 and banned from 1 January 2038.
Registration is refused; selling an unregistrable new car as new is an offence, fine $5,000.
The bill was introduced on 3 March 2026, passed on 18 June 2026 by a large cross-party majority, and enacted on 30 June 2026.
a charge of $250 a year is levied on each battery-electric passenger car from 1 January 2035, paid by its owner, collected with the annual registration renewal and paid to the general budget.
Plug-in hybrids, which pay fuel excise, are exempt from the charge.
The bill was introduced on 3 March 2026, passed on 18 June 2026 by a large cross-party majority, and enacted on 30 June 2026.

context: About 25,000 of them are imported used from Drevland, the larger neighbor to the south (about 3.5 million used-car sales a year), which has no ban and no announced date.
Fuel excise is $0.70 a liter, about $600 a year for an average combustion car, and raises about $2.6 billion a year for the general budget.
record.name: Vessmark Clean Cars Act

readings: U1-a: previously registered in Vessmark: a car first registered in Vessmark after 2035 is new whatever its age, so used combustion cars imported from abroad can no longer be registered
U1-b: previously registered anywhere: a used combustion car registered in Drevland can still be imported and registered after 2035, and so can a new one registered in Drevland first
unclear.text: Whether a used car imported from abroad after 2035 counts as a new passenger car: 'not previously been registered' (section 2) does not say registered where.
